_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
The test shrinks the app's tail-first mounting so that a 15-turn conversation at /c/{{SLUG}} spans many chunks: on load only the last few chunks mount (as ".messages-chunk" elements) and older history renders as placeholders ([data-testid="pending-chunk"]). "The counts" are pending = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="pending-chunk"]').length and mounted = document.querySelectorAll('.messages-chunk').length. "The gap" is the messages container's (".messages-container") scrollHeight - scrollTop - clientHeight. To "open the conversation", navigate to /c/{{SLUG}}, wait for the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) to be visible (allow 30s), then wait until the LAST element matching [data-testid="message"] is visible (its getBoundingClientRect() has a non-zero width and height; allow 30s). The test has already set the shelley.tailFirstTest knob; do not set it yourself. Check every assertion with an eval that has "expect" (or an assert_* or wait_* step): an eval without "expect" asserts nothing. Wait with such steps and a timeout, not with polling loops inside the expression. When a step says to record something, do it in one eval without "expect" that stores it in the named window variable, then check that variable in a separate eval with "expect". Perform the steps in order. Tail-first mounting mounts only the tail at load and keeps the bottom pinned; the background sweep is off.
1. Open the conversation.
2. Right away, in a single eval (no expect), record window.__atLoad = JSON.stringify({pending: pending > 0, mounted: mounted > 0, bottom: gap < 5}) from the counts and the gap at that moment.
3. window.__atLoad must be exactly {"pending":true,"mounted":true,"bottom":true}: placeholders stand in for older history, the tail is real content, and the viewport sits at the true bottom (not merely near it).
4. The last [data-testid="message"] element must intersect the viewport (its bounding rect overlaps both the window and the messages container's rect).
5. The scroll-to-bottom button (".scroll-to-bottom-button") must not be visible.

steps.expression: (function() { var msgs = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="message"]'); var last = msgs[msgs.length - 1]; if (!last) return false; var r = last.getBoundingClientRect(); return r.width > 0 && r.height > 0; })()

(function() { var pending = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="pending-chunk"]').length; var mounted = document.querySelectorAll('.messages-chunk').length; var mc = document.querySelector('.messages-container'); var gap = mc ? mc.scrollHeight - mc.scrollTop - mc.clientHeight : 9999; window.__atLoad = JSON.stringify({pending: pending > 0, mounted: mounted > 0, bottom: gap < 5}); })()

(function() { var msgs = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="message"]'); var last = msgs[msgs.length - 1]; if (!last) return false; var lr = last.getBoundingClientRect(); var mc = document.querySelector('.messages-container'); var mcr = mc ? mc.getBoundingClientRect() : {left:0, top:0, right:window.innerWidth, bottom:window.innerHeight}; var overlapX = lr.left < mcr.right && lr.right > mcr.left; var overlapY = lr.top < mcr.bottom && lr.bottom > mcr.top; var inViewX = lr.left < window.innerWidth && lr.right > 0; var inViewY = lr.top < window.innerHeight && lr.bottom > 0; return overlapX && overlapY && inViewX && inViewY; })()
